findings.title: Password check bypassed when totpCode is supplied with backupCode
findings.body: In `authorize`, password verification is gated by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`. The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is evaluated afterwards. An attacker can send both `totpCode` (any dummy value) and `backupCode`: the first condition is false so no password is verified, the second branch is true so login succeeds on backup-code alone. Backup-code login then becomes single-factor instead of password + backup code, violating the 2FA contract.

findings.title: Throwing instead of returning 500 breaks error contract
findings.body: When encryption key is missing or twoFactorSecret is missing/invalid the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of `return res.status(500).json(...)`. An uncaught throw in a Next.js API route results in a generic 500 HTML/unhandled rejection, not the `{error: ...}` JSON the client (`DisableTwoFactorModal`) expects. The UI will show generic failure and logs leak, and the same pattern is repeated for the backup-code path.

findings.title: Backup-code verification is case-sensitive and crashes on non-string
findings.body: Login does `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` and `indexOf` directly. Generated codes in `setup.ts` are lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`) displayed as `XXXXX-XXXXX`, but user input in uppercase or with surrounding whitespace will not match and returns IncorrectBackupCode. Worse, if `backupCode` is an array/object (truthy), `.replaceAll` throws and crashes authorize instead of returning an error code.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption has read-then-write race allowing reuse
findings.body: Login reads decrypted `backupCodes`, finds the index, sets `backupCodes[index]=null` and writes back with a separate `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both read the same array before either writes, so the same single-use code can be used twice. Single-use codes need an atomic compare-and-set/transaction or DB-level guard.
